notes: Ten turns, all of them starting on this page. The page opens inside a speech already under way (a technical answer about the consumer judge and jurisdiction) that ends at 'Creo que con esto están contestados esos tres planteos.', so that speech is not listed. The three 'Sr. Costa.-' labels that follow the two stenographer's notes are genuine separate turns under rule 2, even though the same man was speaking before each one — the label is printed, so the turn restarts. The two italic dashed lines about manifestations off-microphone stand as their own paragraphs, so they are events; the second one wraps across two printed lines and I joined it into one string. Genuinely odd and worth a maintainer's eye: the interjections labelled 'Sr. Presidente (Petcoff Naidenoff).-' are plainly adversarial cross-examination of the secretary of Commerce ('han fracasado', 'Claro, con los números', 'Sí, “métale” tranquilo'), which reads like an opposition senator rather than a chair; and the chair earlier on the page is a different man, 'Sr. Presidente (Fuentes)'. Either the chair really changed hands with no stenographer's note marking it — there is none printed on this page — or the stenographer attached the office to the wrong man. I recorded both labels exactly as printed and invented nothing. Note also that the chair label here carries a surname, unlike the bare 'Sr. PRESIDENTE.-' usual before 2016. Minor printing detail: the record prints 'la Secretaria de Comercio' without the accent on 'Secretaría' in Costa's last turn, and uses straight quotes round "este es el fuero específico" in the opening paragraph while using curly quotes round “métale” lower down.
